title: Slider Signal Function Autogenerates With Shadowed Variable
body:
### Tested versions

Found it in 4.6, not sure how to find further decimal points to specify which version I have.

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

Category 'complaint' rather than 'problem' here. I used the right-hand Signals panel to hook up a volume slider with it's own value changed signal, and it gave me the following function which I filled with very simple contents, running a function off an autoload:
```
func _on_value_changed(value: float) -> void:
	Audiodirectory.changemusicvolume(value)
```

It then proceeded to complain that I had shadowed the built-in `value` variable. Removing `value: float` from the definition stopped the function from working, though, even though that's a totally autonomous function and `value` is supposedly built-in. Renaming the variable is the only way to clear the warning, which feels a little silly given that's the wording it gave me... It'd be nice if it either didn't use the wording that would shadow the variable, or knew better than to moan about a decision it made, y'know?

### Steps to reproduce

Try to use the Signals panel to make an HSlider node run code when its value changes. It should spit out `func _on_value_changed(value: float) -> void:` and then be angry about it. Alternatively, open MRP and see it already there.
